plants.name: Rosa rugosa
plants.description: A tough, sweetly perfumed shrub with crinkled, deep-green leaves. It is covered in wide, silky-petalled blooms with a boss of golden stamens. Later the flowers give way to glossy, tomato-like red hips.
plants.bloomingSeason: June to September in the Northern Hemisphere, so mid-June falls at the start of its long season
plants.location: Native to the coasts of northeastern China, Japan, Korea and southeastern Siberia. Widely grown in gardens across temperate North America and Europe.
plants.funFact: Rugosa roses thrive on salty sand dunes, where most roses would struggle. Their vitamin C-rich hips are used in jams, teas and syrups.

plants.name: Banksia marginata
plants.description: A hardy shrub or small tree with dark green leaves that are silvery underneath. It holds up upright, lemon-yellow flower spikes that look like bottlebrushes. In the cool of the Southern Hemisphere's winter they are alive with honeyeaters and native bees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mostly February to June, so mid-June falls at the tail end of its flowering period
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, Tasmania and nearby coastal and woodland areas
plants.funFact: Each Banksia spike is made up of hundreds of tiny individual flowers. After flowering, the spikes develop woody seed follicles that often open fully only after bushfire.
